summary: MCP discovery, router, read, search, package-scoped tool-doc read, wiki hygiene, docs-policy, contract-manifest, authoring-ergonomics report, and worker-delivery (commit, submit-for-review) tools.

tools.notes: Bounded catalog paging. total_count is the complete role/tier-visible set; returned_count is this page; truncated_count is what remains after offset. Repeat with offset:next_offset and unchanged filters until has_more:false. A caller limit never relaxes the server byte bounds. Use describe for known-tool detail and query for a known task or name.
use_when: Browse the complete role/tier-visible catalog from an unknown starting tool.
do_not_use_when: An exact tool_name or task_id is known; use workspace_tools_describe or workspace_tools_query.
authoritative_for: current session role/tier-visible registered tool inventory

tools.notes: Targeted detail for a known tool or narrow set. Compact is the default; verbose:true restores the complete descriptor entry. Use list for catalog paging and query for a known task or name.
use_when: Inspect complete metadata for a known tool_name.
do_not_use_when: The tool name is unknown; page workspace_tools_list or filter workspace_tools_query first.

tools.notes: Filtered lookup for one known task_id or exact tool_name. It returns full entries by default; verbose:false selects compact rows. Use list when neither selector is known and describe for one tool's detail.
use_when: Filter by one known task_id or exact tool_name.
do_not_use_when: Neither selector is known; page workspace_tools_list first.
authoritative_for: filtered descriptor lookup by controlled task id or exact tool name

recommended_first_call.operation: query with exactly one known selector

tools.summary: Compact read-only first-tool router for uncertain repo-agent tasks.
tools.notes: Read-only MCP router for unsure tool choice. Given a task description and optional initiative, unit, role, monitor handle, or known resources, returns matched/ambiguous/unknown guidance with recommended first tool, suggested arguments when derivable, do-not-start-with entries, allowed next calls, and a short reason. It does not dispatch, mutate, lint, or read full records; the full routing vocabulary lives in packages/wiki-core/data/tool-routing-intents.v1.json.
use_when: The caller is unsure which repo tool to call first for a coordination, retrieval, dispatch, monitoring, lint, docs, or work-record task.
A task appears to be starting with a broad search/read path but may have a compact structured first tool.
do_not_use_when: The correct authoritative tool and exact arguments are already known.
The task needs the actual canonical record body, dispatch action, mutation, lint run, or generated artifact; call the authoritative tool after routing guidance instead.
requires_prior_state: A short task description or one known identifier such as initiative, unit, role, or monitor_handle.

tools.notes: Read-only agent-safe MCP route for byte-range reads from server-side response content references. Oversized tool results spill the complete JSON payload to the wiki-mcp runtime state directory and return a bounded preview plus a ref_id; callers use this tool with offset and length, base64-decode each data_base64 range, and concatenate bytes to reassemble the complete payload losslessly without carrying an oversized stdio frame.

Read-only MCP route that returns the shared wiki contract manifest (conventions, lint, schema, taxonomy, retrieval, query, and template references) from the checked-in contract tree. Takes no caller arguments and no caller-supplied filesystem root; the manifest is provenance/reference data, not authority to act.
Operator-only new-repository enrollment. Creates required wiki surfaces and syncs the shared contract into the explicitly supplied target.
use_when: Operator is enrolling a new target repository into the shared wiki contract.
do_not_use_when: Routine agent work or an already-enrolled repository; use the owning read, lint, generate, or sync route.

tools.notes: Operator-only contract synchronization or drift check for an explicitly supplied target repository.
use_when: Operator is synchronizing or checking the shared contract in a selected repository.
do_not_use_when: Routine wiki generation or lint; use workspace_generate_and_lint or workspace_lint_repo.

recommended_first_call.operation: sync or check selected repository contract

tools.notes: Reserve the next identifier for a core wiki type in an explicitly selected directory.
use_when: Operator must reserve a core wiki identifier for a direct-directory workflow.
do_not_use_when: A structured workspace create route can allocate the identifier as part of creation.

tools.notes: Create a wiki record in an explicitly selected directory, consuming a reserved or sequential identifier.
use_when: Operator is using the direct-directory record-creation contract.
do_not_use_when: A configured workspace alias is available; use workspace_create_record.

do_not_use_when: A configured workspace alias is available; use workspace_read_page.

use_when: Operator is using the direct-directory record-read contract.
do_not_use_when: A configured workspace alias is available; use workspace_get_record.

tools.notes: Lint an explicitly selected directory against the shared wiki contract.
use_when: Operator is linting through the direct-directory compatibility surface.

use_when: Operator needs generation-only behavior through the direct-directory surface.
do_not_use_when: The task requires generation plus lint; use workspace_generate_and_lint.

use_when: Operator is using the direct-directory generate-and-lint contract.
do_not_use_when: A configured workspace alias is available; use workspace_generate_and_lint.

use_when: Operator explicitly requested the direct-directory persisted-index writer.
do_not_use_when: The task only needs search; use workspace_search_repo, which reads through a missing index.

do_not_use_when: A configured workspace alias is available; use workspace_search_repo.

tools.notes: Preferred MCP search surface for repo-scoped wiki and docs lookup; compact and preview-oriented by default. For a full page or canonical record body use workspace_read_page or workspace_get_record instead. CLI fallback: `npm run wiki -- search --query <query> --json`.
use_when: docs_lookup
do_not_use_when: initiative_status
initiative_next_action
dispatch_readiness
dispatch_role_call
selected_work_record_context when WK-* is known
selected_slice_detail when WK-*#SLICE-* is known

tools.notes: Write-capable MCP route that builds or refreshes the lexical wiki/docs search index for a configured workspace repository — the explicit index-builder companion to workspace_search_repo. Pass reindex:true for a full rebuild. Resolves the repository through configured aliases and accepts no caller-supplied filesystem root. CLI fallback: `npm run wiki -- build-search-index`.

Preferred MCP known-path read surface for repo-relative Markdown, canonical WK JSON, and exact registered IN/DEC JSON paths. Compact canonical IN/DEC results are losslessly recoverable through this existing route by requesting include_record: true with the executable acknowledgement accept_full_read: true; this does not grant arbitrary JSON or filesystem reads. Graph-evidence sidecars at wiki/work-records/evidence/WK-####.graph.json use compact format graph-evidence-sidecar and are replay/debug data, never dispatch authority; selected_slice and selected_record provide bounded detail.
use_when: docs_lookup with known repo path
canonical initiative or decision read with exact registered JSON path
selected_slice_detail with selected_slice:<slice-id>
do_not_use_when: initiative_status
initiative_next_action
dispatch_readiness
dispatch_role_call
selected_work_record_context first call
requires_prior_state: known repo-relative Markdown path, exact registered canonical record path, or known WK plus selected_slice selector

tools.notes: Read one package-owned documentation reference that this session already advertises for a tool it can already see. Verbose discovery projects a scope-qualified doc_references entry naming this route; pass that tool_name and logical path back to get the bytes. Hidden tool names, unadvertised paths, absolute paths, traversal, an absent or mismatched documentation carrier, and a package-version mismatch refuse with typed diagnostics. The route never browses the package, never falls back to the consuming workspace, and never discloses installation roots. Workspace-owned references keep using workspace_read_page.
use_when: docs_lookup for an advertised package-scoped tool documentation reference
do_not_use_when: reading a workspace-owned repository page
browsing arbitrary package or workspace files
requires_prior_state: a verbose workspace_tools_describe or workspace_tools_query result carrying doc_references for the selected tool

tools.notes: Preferred MCP canonical-record read surface for durable WK and registered IN/DEC IDs. Compact canonical IN/DEC results are losslessly recoverable through this existing route by requesting include_record: true with the executable acknowledgement accept_full_read: true; this does not grant arbitrary JSON or filesystem reads. Tracker WK selectors remain available for bounded slice detail.
use_when: canonical initiative or decision payload is needed by durable id
selected_work_record_context after compact summary needs canonical payload
selected_slice_detail after compact summary needs raw/debug payload
do_not_use_when: initiative_status
initiative_next_action
dispatch_readiness
dispatch_role_call
docs_lookup without known durable id
selected_work_record_context first call
selected_slice_detail first call
requires_prior_state: known durable WK, IN, or DEC id and context justifying canonical payload

tools.notes: Write-capable agent-safe MCP route that regenerates the non-canonical wiki views and then lints the configured workspace repository; use after structural wiki changes. Optional max_findings bounds returned findings (omit for the compact default, 0 for counts only, or a positive integer with no hard upper bound; large caps can produce large responses). The set-status/set-closure review/done transitions run this path automatically and surface its result as an advisory closeout_lint summary. CLI fallback: `npm run wiki -- generate-and-lint`.

use_when: A caller needs read-only validation of a configured workspace repository against the shared wiki contract.
do_not_use_when: Generated wiki views must be refreshed before validation; use workspace_generate_and_lint instead.
tools.notes: Read-only agent-safe MCP route that validates a configured workspace repository against the shared wiki contract without writing views, caches, or records; use workspace_generate_and_lint when views must be refreshed first. Optional max_findings bounds returned findings (omit for the compact default, 0 for counts only, or a positive integer with no hard upper bound; large caps can produce large responses).

Explicit opt-in MCP route for repairing only missing docs backlink comments in canonical docs pages. It is separate from read-only workspace_lint_repo and from workspace_generate_and_lint, which remain non-autofixing. The route recomputes fresh lint findings internally, only applies structured missing_docs_backlink findings after docs-root revalidation, and never accepts caller-supplied findings as write authority; optional path/id/comment inputs are narrowing filters only.

Structured docs-policy validator that detects agent-facing non-MCP role-dispatch authority drift; operator/internal sections classified by heading are audience-scoped and do not automatically fail. CLI fallback: `npm run wiki -- docs-policy validate --json`.

Read-only agent FAQ served from the agent-faq.v1 known-issues corpus; each entry pairs a recurring symptom and cause with the exact structured workspace_* route(s) to resolve it and the responsible actor (agent vs operator). Returns all entries by default; pass id for one entry or related_code to filter by a runtime-blocker code. Output is tier-projected: free/local responses show only source-available coordination routes and omit paid/CCE remediation routes and next actions, which appear only under a valid paid/CCE key posture. Accepts no caller-supplied filesystem root. CLI fallback is operator-only.

tools.summary: Read-only compact authoring-ergonomics summary over one bounded evidence source, with an authenticated immutable snapshot for typed inspection. Advisory evidence only.
use_when: turning a repository's fixed errors.log failure journal into typed ERG findings, causal clusters, and conformance evidence
evaluating a retained authoring-ergonomics-retained-smoke.v1 envelope against the four authoring-ergonomics conformance identities
asking which canonical work record owns the producer boundary a cluster was attributed to
do_not_use_when: a verdict, admission decision, or gate is wanted - every result here is advisory evidence
an arbitrary log path, alternate filename, or installation root must be analyzed - only the configured repository's fixed errors.log is resolvable
canonical record ownership must be asserted from a degraded or stale lookup
authoritative_for: compact authoring-ergonomics advisory summary and immutable snapshot creation over one closed evidence source
requires_prior_state: for source_kind workspace_errors_log: nothing - the repository's fixed errors.log is resolved by the server
for source_kind retained_smoke_evidence: a complete authoring-ergonomics-retained-smoke.v1 envelope
tools.notes: Journal first call: {"source_kind":"workspace_errors_log"} reads fixed errors.log and accepts no caller path. source_kind retained_smoke_evidence requires the complete bounded envelope documented by the operation reference. The compact response returns one immutable snapshot and one workspace_authoring_ergonomics_report_query next call, never finding rows, episodes, clusters, raw events, an old full response, or report-local spill. Failure-only evidence remains unevaluable. Routing remains owner_resolved, owner_unresolved, or lookup_degraded.

tools.summary: Read-only typed paging and selected-field inspection over one authenticated immutable authoring-ergonomics snapshot. Advisory evidence only.
use_when: retrieving coverage, workflow, episode, metric, finding, cluster, axis, conformance, owner-routing, or diagnostic rows omitted from the compact report
selecting one stable finding identity or enumerating all findings with exact total, returned, remaining, and continuation accounting
continuing a page using the authenticated cursor returned by this operation
do_not_use_when: no snapshot identity has been returned by workspace_authoring_ergonomics_report
an expired retained-smoke snapshot is unavailable after restart when the caller cannot reattach the original bounded envelope; no incomplete report call is emitted
raw workspace access, a whole legacy response, or a live reread across pages is wanted
a mutation, lifecycle action, admission decision, or policy verdict is wanted
authoritative_for: typed non-authorizing retrieval from one immutable authoring-ergonomics snapshot
requires_prior_state: a current snapshot identity and executable query continuation returned by workspace_authoring_ergonomics_report
the source_kind used to create that snapshot; retained-evidence recovery is callable only while the original bounded envelope remains available

tools.notes: Closed-input worker delivery primitive hosted by the launcher-owned wiki-MCP server. Accepts no caller-supplied fields; the server resolves the frozen per-run binding (write_scope, subject, worktree identity, base_sha, and output branch) from launcher-owned state. No transport credential, path, ref, branch, Git API, shell, or writer selector is exposed. Access is the central session-role-tool-access policy (worker), not this descriptor row.

Worker/reviewer/redteam affordance: move the launcher-assigned WIKI_MCP_ASSIGNED_UNIT to review status. Accepts no caller-supplied unit, status, or other fields. Access is the central session-role-tool-access policy, not this descriptor row.
